paper_title: MathOdyssey Benchmarking Mathematical Problem-Solving Skills in Large   Language Models Using Odyssey Math Data
caption: Mathematical problems across educational levels. We curate and categorize problems by difficulty and subject area.
model_annotation: This pie chart visually represents the distribution of mathematical problems across different educational levels and subject areas as curated for the MathOdyssey benchmark, with each slice corresponding to a specific category and its proportion of the total. The chart contains ten distinct slices, each labeled with the subject, educational level, percentage share, and the count of problems. The largest segment is “Algebra – Olympiad-level” at 21.19% (82 problems), followed by “Combinatorics – Olympiad-level” at 9.56% (37 problems), and “Algebra – High School” at 17.83% (69 problems). Other significant portions include “Pre-Calculus – High School” at 14.21% (55 problems) and “Geometry – Olympiad-level” at 6.46% (25 problems), which is equal in size to “Linear Algebra and Abstract Algebra – University-level” at the same percentage. The remaining categories—“Number Theory – Olympiad-level” (1.03%, 4 problems), “Geometry – High School” (3.62%, 14 problems), “Calculus and Analysis – University-level” (6.20%, 24 problems), “Probability – University-level” (5.43%, 21 problems), and “Statistics – University-level” (4.39%, 17 problems)—are smaller and collectively make up the remainder of the pie. Each slice is color-coded and includes a percentage and count, with no visual emphasis such as exploded sections, and the segments are arranged in a roughly descending order by size from left to right.
